# order: EO:2225  (WPA 1944: 1915 July 22)
# WPA summary: Certain described lands in Mono County, Calif.,reserved for the use of a small band of Paiute Indians as a cemetery and camping ground. IV K 1016.
# book: Kappler, Indian Affairs: Laws and Treaties, vol. IV (Laws, compiled to March 4, 1927; GPO 1929)
# scanned image 690, printed page 1016; page lines 6-20
# source: https://archive.org/download/bwb_S0-DZH-184_4/bwb_S0-DZH-184_4_djvu.xml  sha256 bc0841b0b8ce533e0ddbe4cab79e6bcd29554d87b99833138be7e9135432653a
# found by: date_and_subject; date 1915-07-22; words mono|small|cemetery|camping
# Government printed copy (OCR of a compilation or report), not the signed original. A lead for the
# original_text step: read it against the scan before use. Exact slice of the page OCR follows.
----- EXACT SLICE -----
Wooprow WILSON.
Tue Warre Hovss, 10 July, 1920.
It is hereby ordered that the NE. 14 of section 11, township 2 south, range 31 east
M. D. M., containing 160 acres, in Mono County, California, be, and the same is
hereby reserved for use of a small band of Paiute Indians living near Benton, Calif-
ornia, as a cemetery and camping ground: Provided, That this order shall not affect
any existing valid rights of any person or persons to the land described.
Woobrow WILSON.
Tue Waite House, 22 July, 1915.
POTRERO AND RINCON.
It is hereby ordered, under authority contained in the act of March 2, 1917
(Public 369), that the period of trust on lands held in trust for the use and benefit
of the Potrero (La Piche or La Jolla) and Rincon Bands or Villages of Indians in
California, which trust expires during the calendar year 1917, be, and is hereby,
extended for a period of ten years from the date of expiration thereof.
